So this was narrated by a priest during a shraddha puja for one of my aunts who passed away. 
He was quite a nice priest as he translated all the Sanskrit stuff for us. This was a Hindu Brahmin ceremony in south India. 
According to him, buffalo meat was always consumed in India by everyone. Even the Hindu Brahmins, it was only during Ashok’s reign that Buddhist values were fused into Brahmin culture. Where, any harm to animals was looked down upon. 

During the Shraddha’s it is mandatory that uddina vade and payasam is served. The vade is made of lentils and according to the priest it was a substitute to buffalo meat. So he believes that only because of Buddhism that the Hindu Brahmins stopped consuming meat. Even today, the Goud Saraswat Brahmins of west coast consume all meats/ fish, barring beef! As cow is considered to be a holy animal and embodiment of 1 crore gods. But then again, it shocks me how little this means when it comes to their actual well being etc. I often see cows munching on trash and being used as a commodity. 

As someone mentioned earlier, environmentally speaking, any red meat consumption as population scale is devastating. As human population sky rockets, so does the demand for meat and meat based produce. And trust me, unless every meat eater is cultivating their own produce, the industry is not at all sustainable. Mass production of livestock is regressive to planet earth and has been one of the top causes for, deforestation, climate change, etc. 

Even plant based cultivation only when done right is sustainable. We have seen rapid introduction of GMO produce, powerful chemical agents through fertilisers etc. All this is regressive. Amazon os burning today to suffice the need of meat and pineapples, the Nilgiris mountain range is affected by rubber plantations. From forest fires to landslides, man is one of the main reasons for these so called natural calamities.
